finding.claim: POST /settings/email is decorated only with @login_optional, so an unauthenticated request reaches set_email(g.uid, ...) with g.uid=None. The route is missing an authentication check that its sibling /settings/password enforces with @login_required.
finding.source: Anonymous HTTP POST to /settings/email with no session cookie (routes.py:34-38)
finding.sink: set_email(g.uid, "new@example.org") at routes.py:37, an account-modifying operation

finding.guards_checked: login_optional only reads the session and never aborts; no per-handler ownership or authorization check; no CSRF check. Contrast login_required at routes.py:11-12 which aborts 401. Impact depends on the set_email implementation, which is not in this repo, so exploitability is unconfirmed; the missing check is confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: none. login_optional (routes.py:19-25) only sets g.uid from the session and never aborts; the handler change_email (routes.py:36-38) performs no ownership or auth check. The only auth guard, login_required (routes.py:8-16, abort at line 12), is not applied to this route.
verdict.reason: An anonymous POST reaches change_email at routes.py:37 via login_optional (routes.py:35, wrapper at lines 21-23) with g.uid=None and no abort, so the missing auth check that /settings/password enforces at routes.py:42 is confirmed; the real impact depends on the set_email stub at routes.py:48, which is outside this repo's logic.

finding.sink: set_password(g.uid, "hunter2") at routes.py:44, a credential-modifying operation

finding.guards_checked: Authentication enforced by login_required (routes.py:11-12). No current-password verification, no input validation, no password-strength policy. The literal "hunter2" is a hardcoded credential, which organization policy prohibits. Every account that uses this endpoint receives the same publicly visible password. Impact on the real set_password is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: login_required (routes.py:11-12) aborts with 401 when no session uid, so only an authenticated session can reach the endpoint. That is a precondition, not a block: any logged-in user can trigger the write. No current-password check, input validation, or policy exists in change_password (routes.py:41-45). set_password (routes.py:52-53) is a stub, so the real effect is unverified.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: change_password (routes.py:41-45) ignores the request and calls set_password(g.uid, "hunter2") at routes.py:44 after only the login_required check at routes.py:11-12, so any authenticated user can set their password to a hardcoded literal. The impact on a real password store is unverified because set_password is a stub at routes.py:52-53, but the hardcoded credential and the missing current-password check are present in the code as claimed.

finding.claim: The state-changing POST routes /settings/email and /settings/password rely only on the session cookie and have no CSRF token or Origin/Referer check. A cross-site form POST from a victim's browser can trigger them, and combined with F2 this can set the victim's password to a known value.
finding.source: Cross-site form POST from an attacker-controlled page while the victim has a valid session cookie (routes.py:34-38 and 41-45)
finding.sink: set_email at routes.py:37 and set_password at routes.py:44, both state-changing

finding.guards_checked: No CSRF token is verified in this file and no Origin/Referer check exists. Cookie SameSite is not configured in this file; modern browsers default to Lax, which blocks cross-site POST cookies, so exploitability depends on the session cookie configuration and browser, which are not in this repo. Unconfirmed until cookie settings are known.

verdict.guard_found: None in routes.py. No CSRF token check or Origin/Referer check exists on the POST routes (routes.py:34-38, 41-45). login_required (routes.py:8-16) and login_optional (routes.py:19-25) only read the session. The only possible mitigation is the browser's default SameSite=Lax handling of the session cookie, and the cookie configuration is not in this repo.
verdict.reason: Every cited line matches the candidate's description (routes.py:13, 37, 44 and the route decorators at 34-35 and 41-42), and the code has no CSRF or Origin check, but whether a cross-site POST carries the session cookie depends on SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE and the browser, and neither appears in routes.py (routes.py:5 defines only the bare Flask app), so exploitability cannot be decided from the repo.
